themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 9 THIS WEEK, a 300% jump from the 2.2 weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown, new vendor activity conflicts, or emerging street vending disputes in CD 205.
evidence: 9 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.32)
300% spike represents statistically significant deviation from baseline
Timing suggests acute change in street vending environment or enforcement activity
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and local businesses about enforcement intensity and recent crackdowns
Check with NYPD and Department of Consumer and Worker Protection for enforcement activity or policy changes this week

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicles Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints jumped to 20 LAST WEEK, a 146% increase from the 8.1 weekly average, indicating a potential uptick in abandoned cars clogging Fordham/University Heights streets.
evidence: 20 derelict vehicle complaints last week vs. 8.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.25)
146% spike above baseline represents sustained emergence of this problem
Aligns with repeated community board budget requests for increased sanitation and equipment resources
reporting_angles: Map derelict vehicle clusters with 311 data to identify hotspots (Grand Concourse, near subway stations)
Interview NYPD Tow and Transportation Bureau about removal backlogs or staffing constraints

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints exploded from near-zero to 3 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO, representing a 2300% statistical anomaly (z-score: 8.69), suggesting widespread street-level deterioration in the district.
evidence: 3 curb condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
2300% spike is among the most dramatic statistical anomalies in the dataset
Indicates acute deterioration of street infrastructure that warrants investigation
reporting_angles: Conduct street survey of curb conditions along major thoroughfares (Grand Concourse, University Avenue, Webster Avenue)
Cross-reference with DOT pothole repair data to assess whether curb damage is being addressed

themes_detail.label: Building/Use Violations Rising
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints doubled to 9 LAST WEEK from a 3.0 weekly baseline, a 200% increase (z-score: 4.0) suggesting potential code enforcement or zoning compliance issues emerging in the district.
evidence: 9 building/use complaints last week vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.0)
200% spike represents significant increase in code violation reports
282 active DOB permits filed in the last 90 days provide context for potential construction/use conflicts
reporting_angles: Review recent DOB building permits to identify which projects may be triggering use complaints
Interview Department of Buildings to understand nature of violations (illegal conversion, unpermitted commercial use, occupancy violations)

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Gaps Persist
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints spiked to 9 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 350% jump from 2.0 weekly average, and Residential Disposal complaints rose 256%, while community board repeatedly requests more sanitation trucks—revealing a systemic collection failure.
evidence: Missed collection: 9 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 3.88, up 350%)
Residential Disposal: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.1, up 256%)
Community board budget requests year-after-year for 'new or increased number of sanitation trucks'—indicates unresolved systemic issue
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about route coverage, truck availability, and staffing for CD 205 collections
Document resident experience: talk to households on streets with missed pickups about backup and living conditions
